brief.headline: The LME is shut for the United Kingdom Summer Bank Holiday, so nothing on the board moved for a third day - but the holiday itself is the story, because it means 28-August was the last August session and August 2026 is now a CLOSED month with final published averages: aluminium's monthly cash mean came in at $3,249.63, up 2.97% on July and the first monthly rise since May, yet it ranked only third of the five metals here behind zinc at +7.76% and copper at +6.12%, and aluminium's average inventory fell 11.0% while copper's fell 22.6% - so on the completed month the metal with by far the biggest supply disruption was comfortably out-performed by two metals that had none.
bullets: WHAT MOVED TODAY: NOTHING ON THE EXCHANGE, AND THE REASON IS A HOLIDAY RATHER THAN A WEEKEND. 31-August is the UK Summer Bank Holiday and the LME is closed, so cash stays $3,222.00, three-month $3,241.00 and warehouse stock 246,725 tonnes - the 28-August print, republished unchanged for a third consecutive day. The curve is still a $19.00 CONTANGO, cash below three-month, and the warehouse line has now been effectively flat for nine sessions. THIS PAGE ALSO CORRECTS ITSELF: yesterday it said the next official would print today at 13:20 London. It will not. It prints TUESDAY 01-SEPTEMBER.

THE HOLIDAY CLOSED THE MONTH, AND THE COMPLETED MONTH IS THE NEW INFORMATION. With 31-August a non-trading day, 28-August was August's final session and the monthly averages are now final rather than month-to-date. Aluminium's August cash mean is $3,249.63 against July's $3,155.98 - up $93.65, +2.97%, and the first monthly average to rise since May after declines in June and July. That is a real turn in the trend of the mean, and it is worth stating plainly before the caveat.

THE CAVEAT IS THE RANKING, AND IT IS NOT FLATTERING. Across the same closed month zinc's average rose +7.76%, copper's +6.12%, aluminium's +2.97%, nickel's +0.65% and lead's +0.59%. Aluminium was the metal on this board with the genuine supply shock - a Gulf smelter at 18% of capacity, the largest alumina refinery outside China at half rate, two force majeures - and it still finished the month beaten better than two-to-one by copper and zinc, neither of which had a disruption story at all. The honest reading is that August's aluminium gain was the industrial cycle lifting everything, not the disruption premium paying out.

WHAT TO WATCH: TUESDAY'S REOPEN, AND FREIGHT. The first official in four days prints Tuesday 01-September against a dollar that closed the week up 0.55% at 99.702 with EUR/USD at 1.15830, versus the 1.16460 LME fixing the 28-August board was settled at - if the whole board opens lower together that is currency, not aluminium. Meanwhile the one physical cost that kept moving is ocean freight: the Baltic Dry closed at 3,186 on 28-August, up 79 points and its SEVENTH consecutive gain, +10.5% on the week from 2,882 on 24-August. Rising freight raises delivered bauxite and alumina costs into refineries and smelters with a lag, and it does so regardless of what the metal price does.

drivers.text: Section 232 is roughly three-quarters of the US duty-paid premium — The statutory rate on aluminium articles is 50%, with derivatives at 25% and Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. Applied to the 28-August LME cash official of $3,222.00 the tariff leg alone is $1,611.00/t, against a US duty-paid premium of roughly $2,094/t - about 77%. Computed instead on August's now-final monthly cash mean of $3,249.63, the tariff leg averaged $1,624.82/t across the month. Either way the conclusion holds: this premium is mostly policy, and only the residual reflects freight, financing and regional tightness. No freight/financing/tightness split is published here because none is publicly assessable without a paid assessment.

drivers.text: The European duty-paid premium has fallen on supply relief, not demand collapse — The Europe duty-paid premium is publicly reported down roughly 18% between May and August 2026, from about $600/t to about $490/t, and the reported attribution is returning supply rather than a demand failure. That is the first hard PRICE evidence that the published restart timetable - EGA at Al Taweelah, Slovalco, Magnitude 7 Metals, Alcoa's completed Portland and San Ciprian restarts - is already being paid for in the physical market rather than merely announced. A premium that falls on supply is a healthier signal than one that falls on demand, but it is still a fall.

Global bauxite flows reached 20 million tonnes in July 2026, up more than 3% year on year, with China-bound volumes up 5% offsetting declines almost everywhere else - and the reported driver is buyers pulling purchases FORWARD ahead of Guinea's expected export restrictions. Volume borrowed from later months is not the same as volume created, and the sensible expectation is a weaker autumn in shipped tonnes. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: MATERIALLY UPDATED THIS RUN, AND THE UPDATE CUTS BOTH WAYS. THE GENUINE PROGRESS: the United States declared the Strait of Hormuz free of Iranian sea mines on Thursday 27-August-2026, after a mine-clearing operation lasting months. That is a verifiable, physical milestone rather than another statement, and it removes the single hardest obstacle to reopening. THE REASON THE FLAG STAYS FLAT AND THE STATUS STAYS CLOSED: clearing mines is necessary, not sufficient. Iran's security council has said both sides agreed on a designated central shipping channel CONDITIONAL on the United States meeting its terms, and those published terms are steep - withdrawal of the US naval blockade, compensation for war damages, unfrozen Iranian assets, lifting of sanctions and a permanent end to the conflict against the regime and its regional allies. None has been met. THE OPERATIONAL FACT, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THIS ROW ASSERTS, IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW QUANTIFIED: three ships transited on 23-August against roughly eighty-five a day in normal conditions. The waterway is open on a chart and shut in practice. The distinguishing test remains a laden commercial vessel completing a transit. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis and https://thehill.com/policy/defense/6021575-iran-oman-hormuz-strait-deal/ CARRIED UNCHANGED ON 31-AUGUST. No new public development over the bank-holiday weekend. The 27-August US declaration that the strait is free of Iranian sea mines remains the last verifiable physical milestone, and Iran's published conditions for reopening - withdrawal of the naval blockade, compensation, unfrozen assets and sanctions relief - remain unmet. Traffic remains negligible. The status flag stays flat because clearing mines is necessary, not sufficient.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor

Suez transits have been recovering toward a two-year high as Red Sea routing risk normalises, which shortens Asia-Europe voyage distances and releases vessel capacity back into the global pool. If the Hormuz corridor plan holds, the two chokepoints normalise together and the freight-length premium built into Asia-Europe and Gulf-Asia aluminium and alumina routes compresses from both ends at once. THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS ON THIS PAGE TODAY AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-WAY ARGUMENT: chokepoint normalisation releases vessel supply, but the Baltic Dry has just risen 7.8% in three publications on Capesize demand. Route length and vessel demand are different variables, and right now they point in opposite directions. This remains a conditional statement, not a forecast.

At the last public marks, Guinea-to-China freight of roughly $35-38/t sits against delivered ore of roughly $70-74/t CIF China - freight is about half the delivered cost of the raw material at the head of the chain. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT AUGUST IS NOW A CLOSED MONTH. 28-August was its final session, so the monthly averages are final rather than month-to-date, and they are published: aluminium cash $3,249.63, copper $14,353.40, nickel $16,765.75, zinc $3,875.13, lead $1,855.05.

ALUMINIUM'S COMPLETED AUGUST AVERAGE ROSE 2.97% - THE FIRST MONTHLY GAIN SINCE MAY - AND STILL RANKED ONLY THIRD OF FIVE. THE COMPLETED AUGUST BOARD, PUBLISHED AND FINAL (LME official cash settlement, monthly mean, Westmetall averages pages): ALUMINIUM $3,249.63 against July's $3,155.98, up $93.65 or +2.97%. COPPER $14,353.40 against $13,525.17, up +6.12%. NICKEL $16,765.75 against $16,657.39, up +0.65%. ZINC $3,875.13 against $3,596.11, up +7.76%. LEAD $1,855.05 against $1,844.09, up +0.59%. AUGUST THEREFORE ENDED A TWO-MONTH SLIDE IN THE ALUMINIUM MONTHLY MEAN - June $3,458.64 and July $3,155.98 were both lower than the month before them, and August is the first monthly average to rise since May. THAT IS THE GOOD NEWS AND IT IS GENUINE. THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART IS THE RANKING: aluminium was the THIRD of five and was beaten by both copper and zinc by a factor of two or more. For a metal that spent the whole of August carrying a Gulf supply premium, a smelter outage at roughly 10% of world capacity, the largest alumina refinery outside China at half rate and two producer force majeures, being out-performed 2:1 by copper and 2.6:1 by zinc is the single most important thing the closed month says. The disruption narrative was real; it was not, on the completed month, worth more than the industrial cycle was worth to metals that had no disruption at all.

THE AVERAGE INVENTORY TABLE FOR THE CLOSED MONTH RANKS ALUMINIUM THE SAME WAY THE PRICE TABLE DOES. THE AVERAGE INVENTORY LINES FOR THE CLOSED MONTH SAY THE SAME THING FROM THE OTHER SIDE. Mean August LME warehouse stock: ALUMINIUM 251,215 t against July's 282,350 t, DOWN 11.0%. COPPER 227,683 t against 294,114 t, DOWN 22.6%. ZINC 94,948 t against 110,753 t, DOWN 14.3%. NICKEL 266,050 t against 272,057 t, DOWN 2.2%. LEAD 418,498 t against 384,396 t, UP 8.9% - the only metal on this board whose average inventory GREW. Set the two tables side by side and the cross-metal read is internally consistent rather than contradictory: copper's average inventory fell twice as fast as aluminium's and its average price rose twice as fast; lead's average inventory was the only one to rise and lead had the weakest average price gain and is the only metal on this page negative year to date. Aluminium sits in the middle of that relationship, not above it. A page that wanted to flatter aluminium would publish the +2.97% and stop; the ranking and the inventory table are published alongside it because they are the part that constrains the conclusion.

THE BALTIC DRY CLOSED AT 3,186 ON 28-AUGUST, UP 79 POINTS AND ITS SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE DAILY GAIN, TAKING IT UP 304 POINTS - 10.5% - FROM THE 2,882 DATED 24-AUGUST. It is the highest level this board has carried and the run is now seven sessions long, which makes it a trend rather than a print. WHY IT MATTERS ON AN ALUMINIUM PAGE, STATED WITHOUT OVERREACH: the Baltic Dry is a dry-bulk freight index, and bauxite and alumina move as dry bulk. Guinea-to-China freight of roughly $35-38/t sits against delivered ore of roughly $70-74/t CIF China, so freight is around half the delivered cost of the raw material at the front of the aluminium chain. A 10.5% weekly move in the benchmark is therefore a real cost signal with a lag, and it is larger than anything the metal price did in the same week. IT IS NOT A DEMAND SIGNAL AND IS NOT PRESENTED AS ONE - the index rises on grain and iron-ore chartering as readily as on bauxite. The honest framing is that it raises the cost floor beneath the metal, which cuts against refinery and smelter margin rather than in favour of it.

GLOBAL BAUXITE FLOWS REACHED 20 MILLION TONNES IN JULY 2026, UP MORE THAN 3% YEAR ON YEAR, WITH CHINA-BOUND VOLUMES UP 5% OFFSETTING DECLINES ACROSS ALMOST EVERY OTHER REGION - AND THE REPORTED REASON IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. The strength is attributed to buyers PULLING PURCHASES FORWARD ahead of Guinea's expected export restrictions, which means July's volume is borrowed from the coming months rather than earned by demand. THE POLICY BACKGROUND IS PUBLIC AND CONSISTENT WITH THAT READING: Guinea has been preparing measures to cap bauxite exports after shipments rose around 25% to 183 million tonnes in 2025 and spot prices fell to roughly $32-38/dmt, a four-year low and less than half the government's stated recovery target. Reported policy design points at an annual cap near 150 million tonnes. WHAT FOLLOWS FOR THE ALUMINIUM CHAIN, WITHOUT SPECULATION: a front-loaded July raises the odds of a weaker autumn in shipped volume, and a binding export cap would push bauxite and therefore alumina costs UP - which is a cost-side risk for refineries and smelters and a margin risk rather than a price-support story. Timing and the final form of the restrictions have not been publicly confirmed, and nothing here should be read as a settled schedule.

CHINA'S ALUMINIUM BILLET INVENTORY FELL TO 139,500 TONNES ON 27-AUGUST, DOWN 5,000 TONNES FROM THE PRIOR MONDAY AND 3,500 TONNES FROM THE PRIOR THURSDAY, ENDING THE CONTINUOUS BUILD-UP AND TURNING TO A DECLINE ON THE WEEK. SMM statistics for major consumption areas also report warehouse withdrawals RECOVERING, which is the demand-side half of the same observation and the more meaningful half - inventory can fall because supply stopped arriving as easily as because buyers turned up, and recovering withdrawals point at the latter. THE OFFSETTING FACT IS PUBLISHED IN THE SAME RELEASE AND IS NOT MINOR: processing fees are described as broadly under pressure across the board. A destocking that happens while conversion margins compress is volume without profitability, so this is a genuine but narrow positive - it addresses the demand doubt that has hung over the Chinese leg of this market all month without yet saying anything good about the economics of serving it. Inventory was also reported 5,500 tonnes higher than the same period comparison, so the level remains elevated even after the draw.

NALCO REPORTED Q1 FY27 NET PROFIT OF RS 2,002.38 CRORE, UP 88% FROM RS 1,063.86 CRORE A YEAR EARLIER, ON REVENUE OF RS 5,302.38 CRORE (+39.01%) AND PROFIT BEFORE TAX OF RS 2,649.66 CRORE (+87.33%). The company also recorded its highest-ever Q1 bauxite excavation at 19.52 lakh tonnes and highest-ever Q1 calcined alumina production at 5.77 lakh tonnes. AN INTEGRATED BAUXITE-TO-ALUMINIUM PRODUCER NEARLY DOUBLING PROFIT ON RECORD VOLUMES IS A DIRECT COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK THESIS, and this run adds NALCO to the earnings-history panel for that reason.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXPORTS ARE REPORTED UP 18.7% YEAR ON YEAR TO JULY, WITH PRODUCERS SHIPPING METAL THAT MUTED DOMESTIC DEMAND WOULD NOT ABSORB, AGAINST BEIJING'S 45 MILLION TONNE OUTPUT CAP. That export surge is the mechanism by which Chinese surplus reaches the seaborne balance, and it has been easing the shortages created by the Middle East conflict. The cap limits domestic expansion and pushes Chinese investment overseas rather than forcing production cuts at home, so the export channel is the one to watch rather than the production number.

ALUNORTE, THE LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA, REMAINS REPORTED AT ROUGHLY HALF CAPACITY ON A NATURAL-GAS SUPPLY FAILURE, WITH HYDRO GUIDING A USD 75-100 MILLION Q3 IMPACT AND TWO FORCE MAJEURES LIVE ON ALUMINIUM SALES. Its joint venture Qatalum, shut on gas shortages, is reported stabilised near 60% of nameplate. Middle East LNG, essential to refining, remains scarce under the tanker blockade. NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND CHANGES EITHER SITUATION and both are physical supply failures rather than price problems.

THE RESTART TIMETABLE IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN FORECAST AND IT LENGTHENED THIS MONTH. Magnitude 7 Metals will restart the No. 1 potline at Marston, Missouri, adding 75,000 t/y with first metal before end-2026; Hydro's Slovalco has agreed terms with the Slovak government to resume 75 kt from Q4-2026. That is 150 kt/y of Western capacity returning inside four months, on top of Century holding 2026 guidance at 630 kt with Mt Holly complete, Alcoa's Portland and San Ciprian restarts done, and EGA's Al Taweelah guided back to pre-war output in Q1-2027 from about 18% of capacity today.

THE CHINESE DEMAND EVIDENCE REMAINS GENUINELY TWO-SIDED AND NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND RESOLVES IT - SMM publishes on Chinese business days and produced no edition newer than 27-August. On the constructive side, three Chinese converters reported H1-2026 growth on 28-August: Lizhong revenue +30.32%, Yinbang +49.10%, Yongjie +18.05%. Against it: Chalco's Q2 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year, cast alloy social inventory has built for three consecutive weeks to 31,800 tonnes, and central China spot traded at an 80-120 yuan/t discount to the SHFE September contract. Peak-season stockpiling has yet to materialise.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS NOW BEEN DEAD FOR NINE SESSIONS AND THE ARITHMETIC IS UNFLATTERING. LME aluminium stock fell from 303,675 tonnes at end-June to 246,925 by 17-August - a 56,750-tonne draw - and has since moved a NET 200 TONNES to 246,725, with three of those sessions printing a change of exactly zero. Two hundred tonnes is 0.08% of the total and roughly three minutes of global primary output. A market in a widening contango with a flat warehouse line is not a tight market, whatever the flat price does.

COPPER REMAINS THE TIGHT METAL ON THIS BOARD AND THE CONTRAST WITH ALUMINIUM IS THE SHARPEST STRUCTURAL SIGNAL AVAILABLE. On the identical 28-August board copper carries a $165.00 BACKWARDATION - cash $14,535.00 over a $14,370.00 three-month - on a stock line that fell another 1,300 tonnes to 234,275, a fifteen-session low. Aluminium carries a $19.00 CONTANGO on a stock line that has not moved in nine sessions. One metal the market will pay $165 to have today; another it will pay $19 to defer.

THE BAUXITE ROW IS CARRIED AT ITS 13-AUGUST SMM WEEKLY BASIS BECAUSE NO NEWER PUBLIC EDITION WAS RETRIEVABLE, AND THE FREIGHT LEG IS WHAT MOVED INSTEAD. At that mark the SMM Imported Bauxite Index was $71.72/mt with Guinea CIF China $70-74/mt and the Guinea August long-term contract settled at $73-74/t. Guinea-to-China freight at roughly $35-38/t is approaching HALF the delivered cost of the ore - so this weekend's 7.8% rise in the Baltic Dry, Capesize-led, acts on delivered bauxite cost even with the ore assessment itself unchanged. Guinea accounts for roughly 73% of global bauxite exports.

CARBON BORDER POLICY AND CERTIFICATION CONTINUE MIGRATING FROM DIFFERENTIATOR TO CONDITION OF MARKET ACCESS. Hindalco's Baphlimali mine became India's first ASI-certified bauxite operation under Performance Standard V3.1, extending a certified chain into roughly 2.67 Mt/yr of alumina. Read alongside the EU's carbon border mechanism and growing low-carbon premium channels, certification is becoming an entry requirement for the highest-value European and downstream channels. A related structural item: the EU tariff increase and the UAE scrap export ban are contracting European and Middle Eastern scrap supply, with China's July scrap imports down to roughly 119,600 tonnes from 133,000 in June.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

That matters for the balance argument because the standard bear case against a high LME is that converters destroy demand; a 23% sales increase with a 24% EBITDA increase is not consistent with that. It also sets the tone into Hindalco's own print on 07-Aug, where management has guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation and the upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters.

earnings.note: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

The company reported its highest-ever Q1 bauxite excavation at 19.52 lakh tonnes and its highest-ever Q1 calcined alumina production at 5.77 lakh tonnes. Added to this board and to the earnings-history panel this run as the designated progressive backfill. NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. Public listed-company disclosure, carried to read the cycle only.

status.name: EGA (Al Taweelah)
status.status: PARTIAL RESTART - ~18% OF CAPACITY; PRE-WAR OUTPUT GUIDED TO Q1-2027
status.update: EGA has set out plans to restore production at the Al Taweelah smelter, shut following an Iranian strike in the early stages of the war. The smelter is reported operating at 18% of capacity and guided to return to pre-war output levels in Q1-2027. The Al Taweelah alumina refinery has been running again since 10-July and alumina production is reported reaching 50% of the refinery's capacity. The region accounted for roughly 10% of global primary production before the conflict, so this is the single largest identified block of returning supply on the board - and it arrives on a published timetable rather than a forecast. UNCHANGED THIS RUN: no newer public disclosure was retrievable at compile time. ADDED THIS RUN, BECAUSE IT SHOWS WHERE THE RESTART IS ALREADY LANDING: the Europe duty-paid premium is publicly reported down roughly 18% between May and August 2026, from about $600/t to about $490/t, with the Al Taweelah alumina refinery restart named as a principal driver alongside European smelter capacity returning at Hydro Slovalco, Alcoa San Ciprian and Nordural Grundartangi. Supply relief reaches the regional premium before it reaches the exchange price.
src: Discovery Alert - Europe aluminium duty-paid premium correction May-August 2026 and the attributed restart drivers; Trading Economics - EGA Al Taweelah restart guidance to pre-war output in Q1-2027

status.name: Norsk Hydro (NHY) / Alunorte / Qatalum
status.status: GAS DISRUPTION - ALUNORTE AT ~50% CAPACITY, Q3 IMPACT GUIDED $75-100m; QATALUM STABILISED NEAR 60% OF NAMEPLATE
status.update: Alunorte in Brazil - the largest alumina refinery outside China - is reported operating at roughly half capacity after its natural-gas supplier reported disruptions, and Hydro has publicly guided the Q3-2026 impact on its Bauxite and Alumina segment at USD 75-100 million. status.name: Slovalco (Hydro) / Magnitude 7 Metals
status.status: NEW RESTARTS CONFIRMED - 75 kt EACH, BOTH LANDING BY OR IN Q4-2026
status.update: NEW ROW THIS RUN. Two further restarts are now on the published record and both are Western capacity. Hydro's Slovalco smelter has agreed terms with the Slovak government to resume production of 75,000 tonnes of aluminium capacity, with production expected to start in Q4-2026. status.name: China operators (aggregate)
status.status: AT THE 45 Mt POLICY CEILING; OUTPUT STABLE, EXPORTS ELEVATED
status.update: Chinese primary output remains constrained by the 45 Mt policy ceiling, but exports rose 18.7% year on year in the twelve months to July as muted domestic demand allowed producers to ship metal. That export surge is the single largest offsetting supply factor against the Gulf outages and the mechanism by which Chinese surplus reaches the seaborne market. The Chinese margin picture is now less comfortable than the volume picture: Chalco's Q2 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year. UNCHANGED ON VOLUMES THIS RUN; the margin observation is new.

status.name: Outside-China aggregate (SMM / AL Circle statistics)
status.status: RISING ON NEW-PROJECT RAMP-UPS AND RESTARTS
status.update: Production resumptions in the Middle East are reported continuing through August alongside new projects in Indonesia and Vietnam ramping up and Balco's expanded capacity, with overseas daily average aluminium production reported up 1.6% month on month. The counterweight in the same statistics is that total outside-China production in July was still down 6.7% year on year, mainly on lower Middle East operating rates - so the level remains depressed even as the direction has turned. Both facts are carried because reporting only one of them would mislead. INDIA IS FOLDED INTO THIS ROW THIS RUN RATHER THAN CARRIED SEPARATELY: both Indian majors continue to publish volume growth and cost reduction as their stated strategy and both reported record recent quarters - Hindalco India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA of RS 7,390 crore in Q1 FY27 and Vedanta Aluminium EBITDA of RS 10,499 crore on the company's standalone quarterly basis - with Hindalco also commissioning India's first superfine precipitated aluminium trihydrate plant. Indian capacity growth is structural supply, not cyclical, and it belongs in the outside-China aggregate rather than in a separate producer row.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY, AND NO CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED ON THIS RUN. The two live structural questions are unchanged in substance. FIRST, THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ: Iran and Oman have confirmed agreement on a temporary maritime route under a phased framework carrying a 30-to-60-day negotiating window toward a permanent corridor plus joint mine clearing, but officials also state the waterway will not fully reopen until the United States fulfils commitments under the lapsed June interim deal, and NO VESSEL HAS TRANSITED - the strait remains effectively closed to commercial shipping. A first transit would be a material change and would trigger a re-rate of the Gulf corridors on this panel; another announcement would not. SECOND, US TRADE POLICY: a material correction is made this run - the 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian goods effective 22-August EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES products already subject to Section 232, including aluminium, so the Canada-to-US corridor carries the Section 232 rate alone at an unchanged 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives. The reported cut in the Canadian Section 232 rate to 25% has never been published. THE CORRIDOR THAT HAS ACTUALLY MOVED VOLUME THIS YEAR IS CHINA OUTBOUND: Chinese aluminium exports rose 18.7% year on year in the twelve months to July as muted domestic demand freed metal for export despite the 45 Mt output cap, and that flow is the principal mechanism offsetting the Gulf shortfall in the seaborne market.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.
src: AL Circle - China eases aluminium shortage after Iran war, but pressure shifts to Western fabricators, 18-Aug-2026

flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June, and on the published aggregate the IAI's June-2026 release (20-July-2026) showed global primary output down 1.5% y/y; a widely repeated 'outside-China -6.7% y/y in July' figure could not be traced to a dated IAI release at this refresh and is not carried here. Transit has been the binding constraint rather than production - but production is also impaired in its own right: EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots on 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar and confirmed still shut in its 04-Aug Q2 disclosure. THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.
src: Bloomberg / Kpler via public reporting - Iran-Oman Hormuz route agreement and transit counts (05-Aug-2026)

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: THE FIRST OFFICIAL IN FOUR DAYS - AND THIS PAGE CORRECTS ITSELF ON THE DATE. Yesterday it said Monday 31-August; 31-August is the UK Summer Bank Holiday and the exchange is shut, so the next official prints TUESDAY 01-SEPTEMBER. TWO SPECIFIC TESTS. FIRST, CURRENCY: the 28-August board was settled against an EUR/USD LME fixing of 1.16460; the weekend close was 1.15830 with the dollar index up 0.55% at 99.702 on hawkish Jackson Hole commentary that lifted September rate-hike odds to roughly 57%. If the whole board opens lower together, that is the dollar and not aluminium. SECOND, CONVERGENCE: on the post-ring contract-for-difference board 28-August closed with zinc -0.46%, nickel -0.62% and lead -0.63% while the LME officials had all five metals higher. If Tuesday's officials converge toward the post-ring board, Friday's rally - and therefore the final data point of the completed August month - was a fixing artefact. WATCH THE SPREAD ALONGSIDE THE PRICE: a contango that widens on a falling price is a materially worse signal than one that widens on a rising one.

THE AVERAGE COLUMN ROLLS. From 01-September the prior-month mean on this page becomes AUGUST rather than July, which lifts the aluminium reference from $3,155.98 to $3,249.63, copper from $13,525.17 to $14,353.40, nickel from $16,657.39 to $16,765.75, zinc from $3,596.11 to $3,875.13 and lead from $1,844.09 to $1,855.05. This is a mechanical roll rather than a market event, but it changes every 'versus average' comparison on the page in one step and is flagged in advance so that the shift is not mistaken for a price move.

SEPTEMBER'S FIRST CHINESE DATA AND THE BILLET DESTOCK TEST. China's aluminium billet inventory in major consumption areas fell to 139,500 tonnes on 27-August, down 5,000 tonnes week on week, ending a continuous build-up, with warehouse withdrawals reported recovering - but with processing fees broadly under pressure. The question the next SMM editions answer is whether that is one week of restocking into a holiday or the start of a genuine demand turn. One week is not a trend and this page will not treat it as one.

GUINEA BAUXITE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS - TIMING AND FORM STILL UNCONFIRMED. Global bauxite flows reached 20 million tonnes in July, up more than 3% year on year, with the strength attributed to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of the expected curbs. Reported policy design points at an annual cap near 150 million tonnes after 2025 shipments of around 183 million tonnes and spot prices at a four-year low of roughly $32-38/dmt. If a cap binds, ore and therefore alumina costs rise - a cost-side event for refineries and smelters rather than a demand event. Nothing has been enacted publicly and no date is confirmed.

SMM WEEKLY FLUORIDE-SALT AND BAUXITE REVIEWS. The input-basket rows for AlF3, cryolite and imported bauxite advance on these publications; the bauxite row has been held at its 13-August basis because no newer public edition has been indexed. New marks are appended to the input history only when they publish - gaps are left as gaps rather than interpolated.

MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Prebaked anode and coal-tar-pitch settlements, and the green petcoke settlements behind the calcined-coke row, publish on a monthly cycle around the 17th-18th. These are the largest single controllable cost line in a smelter after power, and they are the rows most likely to add a new history point in the coming fortnight.

THE JAPANESE Q4-2026 PREMIUM ROUND HAS NOT OPENED PUBLICLY. Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July. This page carries a $310-400/t scenario range rather than a number, held unchanged for a fourth run. The range is wide because the Gulf supply premise is unresolved: mines declared cleared on 27-August, waterway still closed, Iranian conditions unmet, transits negligible. A number will exist when the round opens.

EGA AL TAWEELAH RETURN TO PRE-WAR OUTPUT. The smelter runs at roughly 18% of capacity and the publicly guided return to pre-war levels is Q1-2027. This is the largest single dated supply event on the board: it restores output from a region that accounted for around 10% of global production before the conflict, and it is the anchor of the supply-relief timetable that has capped this market since March.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD, AND THE COMPLETED AUGUST MONTH IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE YET THAT IT IS ALREADY BEING PAID FOR. The timetable is public: EGA restoring Al Taweelah from about 18% of capacity toward pre-war output in Q1-2027, Hydro's Slovalco resuming 75 kt from Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals restarting the No. 1 potline at Marston, Missouri for 75 kt/y by end-2026, Century holding 2026 guidance at 630 kt with Mt Holly complete, Alcoa's Portland and San Ciprian restarts done, Tomago underwritten beyond 2028 by an A$2.5bn Australian package. THE PRICE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY THERE - the Europe duty-paid premium is publicly reported down roughly 18% from about $600/t in May to about $490/t in August, attributed to supply relief rather than demand collapse. THE NEW EVIDENCE IS THE CLOSED MONTH ITSELF: with roughly a tenth of world capacity impaired, aluminium's monthly average still rose only 2.97% against zinc's 7.76% and copper's 6.12%, and its forward curve averaged a $1.60 contango across all twenty sessions. A market expecting sustained scarcity does not produce that combination. The trend is UP because each additional dated restart tightens the cap.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED AND NINE SESSIONS NOW CONFIRM IT. LME aluminium stock went from 303,675 tonnes at end-June to 246,925 by 17-August, a 56,750-tonne draw, and has since moved a NET 200 TONNES to 246,725 across nine sessions, three of which printed a change of exactly zero. Two hundred tonnes is 0.08% of the total and roughly three minutes of global primary output. A rally with no draw and a WIDENING contango is a positioning rally, and the correct inference is that the tightness argument at the LME front end is not currently supported by the inventory data. TREND HELD AT UP, AND THE WEEKEND ADDS ONE PIECE OF INDIRECT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN NONE: the rates repricing that hit after Friday's ring raises the carry cost of holding inventory, which bears on a curve already in a $19.00 contango. Financing metal gets more expensive precisely when the curve pays least to defer it - that combination discourages the stock-building that would end the stall, and it argues the flat line persists rather than resolves.

GULF SUPPLY DISRUPTION PERSISTS BUT HAS STOPPED BEING PAID FOR - HELD FLAT DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN DOWNGRADED. The physical facts are unchanged and remain serious: EGA's Al Taweelah runs at roughly 18% of capacity with pre-war output guided only to Q1-2027, the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to commercial traffic with transits at three on 23-August against roughly eighty-five a day normally, and Iran's published conditions for reopening are unmet. The 27-August United States declaration that the waterway is mine-free is a genuine physical milestone and removes an obstacle without removing the dispute. WHAT THE COMPLETED MONTH ADDS is that the market spent all of August with these facts in front of it and still produced a $1.60 average contango and a third-of-five price ranking. The risk has not gone away; the compensation for it has. Flat, not down, because an unresolved chokepoint can reprice violently in either direction on a single headline.

PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON. TREND HELD AT DOWN, BUT WITH A NEW QUALIFICATION THAT CUTS THE OTHER WAY. The evidence that moved this row down remains intact: three Chinese aluminium processors reported growing H1-2026 results on 28-August - Lizhong revenue RMB 18.822bn (+30.32%) with net profit RMB 577m (+43.81%); Yinbang revenue RMB 4.27bn (+49.10%) with net profit RMB 88.538m (+95.08%); Yongjie revenue RMB 5.225bn (+18.05%) with net profit ex-non-recurring items RMB 247m (+31.12%). These are audited half-year converter numbers, not survey sentiment, and they are hard to reconcile with a thesis that physical demand is failing. THE NEW QUALIFICATION IS CHALCO: Q2-2026 attributable net profit fell 26.2% year on year on revenue down 1.9%, in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200. Converters growing while the largest integrated upstream producer earns less is a coherent picture - margin migrating down the chain - but it is not the picture of uniformly strong demand. The row stays DOWN because the converter evidence is the more direct read on physical offtake, and the counter-evidence is disclosed rather than omitted. What remains unresolved from SMM's 27-August meeting is that peak-season stockpiling had YET TO MATERIALISE, with cast alloy social inventory building for a third week to 31,800 tonnes and central China spot at an 80-120 yuan/t discount to the SHFE September contract.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND HELD AT FLAT, AND THE COMPLETED WEEK REMAINS THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE AVAILABLE: aluminium finished at $3,222.00 against $3,227.00 five sessions earlier, a 0.16% loss, having round-tripped three times inside a $39.50 range without breaking either end of it. That is consistent with a position base already substantially cleared and now churning rather than one still to be cleared. ONE OBSERVATION IS ADDED THIS RUN AND IT CUTS MILDLY IN ALUMINIUM'S FAVOUR: on the contract-for-difference board that trades past the London close, 28-August closed with zinc, nickel and lead all LOWER while aluminium alone held a gain at +0.28%. When a macro shock hits the whole complex and one metal holds, that is usually a sign of lighter rather than heavier positioning in it. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS UNCHANGED: no public positioning data was retrievable this run and the read is inferential. What would change it is a break of the 20-August low at $3,183.00 on the three-month, which has now held on six consecutive sessions.

INPUT-COST INFLATION THROUGH FREIGHT AND BAUXITE - RAISED THIS RUN AND THE TREND IS UP. Dry-bulk freight has risen for seven consecutive sessions to 3,186 on the Baltic Dry, up 10.5% on the week from 2,882. Bauxite and alumina move as dry bulk and, at the last public marks, Guinea-to-China freight of roughly $35-38/t sits against delivered ore of roughly $70-74/t CIF China - freight is about half the delivered cost of the raw material at the head of the chain. Layered on top, global bauxite flows were pulled forward into July, up more than 3% to 20 million tonnes with China-bound volumes up 5%, explicitly ahead of Guinea's expected export restrictions; a binding cap near a reported 150 million tonnes a year would lift ore and therefore alumina costs. THE PARTIAL OFFSET IS ENERGY: Brent lost more than 5% on the week and European TTF gas fell 2.63%, which lowers smelter power and refining costs. The two do not cancel cleanly and this page does not pretend they do. Trend UP because the freight move is a seven-session trend and the bauxite policy risk is one-directional.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE. TREND HELD AT DOWN, AND A CORRECTION TO YESTERDAY'S COAL FIGURE IS MADE EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN QUIETLY. Across the completed week the energy complex eased: Brent posted a weekly loss of MORE THAN 5% and finished at $88.29 (-0.26%), WTI at $83.44 (-0.11%), and European TTF gas fell 2.63% to EUR 66.47/MWh, giving back Thursday's spike in full. Gas is the direct input to alumina refining and a large input to European smelter power, so the TTF reversal is the more important of the two. THE CORRECTION: yesterday this row carried thermal coal as up 6.29% in a single session to $139.50. Today's board carries coal at $139.75 with a DAY change of +0.18% and a MONTH change of +7.33%, and the single-session figure published here yesterday is not reproducible against it. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION AND IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT FLAGGED MORE STRONGLY DOWN: coal is up more than 7% on the month at a nine-week high, and coal is the dominant power input for the Chinese smelters that produce roughly 60% of world primary aluminium. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS UNCHANGED: none of the energy easing has yet appeared in any published coke, pitch or anode mark - no CPC, green coke, CTP or prebaked anode figure newer than mid-August was publicly retrievable - and coal tar pitch at its 13-August mark of roughly 4,960 yuan/t is still up from 4,705 on 23-July. Petroleum coke is a refinery co-product loosely tethered to the crude complex, so a softer crude week is disinflationary for the carbon leg with a lag rather than immediately.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM, AND THE RISK IS THAT PRICED-IN RELIEF DOES NOT ARRIVE. TREND HELD AT UP AND THE PUBLIC RECORD IS NOW GENUINELY CONFLICTED, WHICH IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY PREFERENCE. THE FACTS THAT ARE NOT IN DISPUTE: the Section 232 rate is verified again this run at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivative articles, applied to the full customs value since 06-April-2026; and the Section 338 duty on Canadian goods effective 22-August EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES products already covered by Section 232, so it does not compound the aluminium position - a correction this board made two runs ago and keeps visible. WHAT IS IN DISPUTE IS WHETHER RELIEF IS COMING: brokers have reported a tentative deal involving reduced tariffs and/or a quota system for aluminium and steel, and a 72-hour implementation delay was announced on 19-August citing progress in talks, but NO proclamation cutting the Canadian rate from 50% to 25% has been published. This board treats an unsigned deal as unsigned, and the risk is precisely that the market has not. The September US Midwest premium slumped 8.2% to 95 cents a pound on 20-August and October-November contracts fell more than 12% pricing relief that has not arrived. At the unchanged 50% rate on the 28-August cash official of $3,222.00 the tariff leg is $1,611.00/t of a roughly $2,094/t duty-paid premium - about 77% - and it is unchanged today only because the metal price is unchanged. A premium that is three-quarters policy re-rates on a signature.

FREIGHT AND DELIVERED-COST INFLATION INSIDE EVERY REGIONAL PREMIUM. TREND HELD AT UP AND THIS RUN IT IS THE BEST-EVIDENCED ROW ON THE REGISTER RATHER THAN THE STALEST. The Baltic Dry Index is 3,107 on its 27-August publication, up 51 points on the day and up 225 points - 7.8% - from the 2,882 dated 24-August that this board carried yesterday. That is the highest level in the publicly published August series; the prior August high was 3,089 on 07-August. THE MOVE IS CAPESIZE-LED, WHICH IS THE SEGMENT THAT CARRIES BAUXITE AND ALUMINA: the Baltic Capesize Index is 5,138, up 105, with average daily capesize earnings at $46,601, up $950 on the day and up $4,496 - 10.7% - since 24-August. Guinea-to-China freight at roughly $35-38/t against delivered ore of $70-74/t means ocean freight is approaching HALF the delivered cost of the bauxite, and Guinea supplies roughly 73% of global bauxite exports, so this is a concentrated route exposure. THE POINT THAT MATTERS AGAINST A HORMUZ NARRATIVE THAT HAS REPRICED REPEATEDLY: dry bulk freight is set by vessel supply and bulk demand, not by one waterway. Neither a reopening nor a continued closure moves Capesize rates. Freight is the stickier of the two costs inside every regional premium and on the newest available print it is rising faster than it was. THE DATE IS DISCLOSED: this is a 27-August publication, one day older than the LME board, because no 28-August print was publicly retrievable at this compile.

CARBON BORDER POLICY AND CERTIFICATION BECOME CONDITIONS OF MARKET ACCESS RATHER THAN DIFFERENTIATORS. TREND HELD AT UP. Hindalco's Baphlimali mine became India's first ASI-certified bauxite operation under Performance Standard V3.1, extending a certified chain into roughly 2.67 Mt/yr of alumina and taking the group to eleven certified sites. Read alongside the EU's carbon border mechanism and the growing low-carbon premium channels, certification is migrating from a marketing claim to an entry requirement for the highest-value European and downstream channels - and demand-side signals point the same way, with Kirin publicly exploring greater use of recycled, GHG-free and low-carbon aluminium in packaging. A related structural item: SMM reports the EU's tariff increase and the UAE's scrap export ban are contracting European and Middle Eastern scrap supply, with China's July scrap imports down to roughly 119,600 tonnes from 133,000 in June - trade policy is reshaping the recycled leg of the chain as well as the primary one. This is a slow risk with a long fuse and it is carried for that reason.

THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
